 Mr. S.S. Alaspurkar, Advocate for appellants  None for respondent Nos.1 and 2  Mr. M.B. Joshi, Advocate for respondent No.3

The present appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short M.V. Act) by the original claimants for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Amravati (for short MACT) in Claim Petition No.410/2010 by judgment dated 29/09/2015.
2. Heard learned Advocate for the Appellants and learned Advocate for the Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.
None for the other Respondents.
With their assistance perused the record.

3. There is no dispute in respect of death of Mr. Nisar Abdul Rahman in the motor vehicle accident dated 24/07/2010 due to involvement of the taxi car and the motorcycle, on which the deceased was travelling.
The appeal is preferred only on the point of quantum.
The learned Tribunal considered the salary of the deceased for the month of June, 2010.

According to the learned Advocate for the Appellants, the accidental death occurred on 24/07/2010 and the salary certificate for the moth of July, 2010 was filed before the learned Tribunal, which could not be exhibited due to inadvertence.
He submits that the salary at the time of death is required to be considered.
He further submits that the learned Tribunal deducted 1/3rd amount from the income of deceased and since the Claimants are five (5) in number, the deduction should be 1/4th.
He submits that the award passed by the learned Tribunal be modified.

4. Learned Advocate for the Insurance Company submits that, the deceased did not work for the entire month of July and therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly considered the salary of previous month.
As regards the deduction is concerned, he fairly submits that, it should be 1/4th as per the settled position.
5. Undisputedly, the salary of the deceased for the Month of June, 2010 is considered by the learned Tribunal as Rs.27,000/- after necessary deductions towards income tax and professional tax.
The record indicates that the Claimants filed on record the necessary documents including the salary certificate dated 11/04/2012 showing the salary of deceased for the month of July, 2010.
There is no serious dispute that, the said salary certificate was filed on record by the Claimants before the learned Tribunal.
There is nothing to discard the said certificate, which is having the signature and stamp of the Principal of the College, in which deceased was working.
Yasmeen Jahan W/O. Nisar Ahmed And ... vs Vinod S/O. Pralhad Dhule And Others on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65839305/
2 6. Perusal of the said salary certificate shows that the gross salary of deceased was Rs.35,890/- and the income tax and the professional tax are shown as Rs.1,500/- and Rs.200/- respectively.
It is settled position under the law that, only deductions towards the income tax, professional tax are to be considered, while computing the compensation.
After deducting the said amount from the salary of July, 2010, the amount of net salary comes to Rs.35,890/-.
Undisputedly, the accidental death of deceased was on 24/07/2010, which goes to show that for a substantial period of month of July the deceased worked.

Therefore, the contention of the learned Advocate for the Insurance Company that, the deceased did not work for the entire month and therefore, he is not entitled to the salary of July has no substance.
It was the salary at the time of accidental death.
7. The learned Tribunal considered the 1/3rd deduction towards dependency.
The claimants are five (5) in number.

As per the decision of the learned Supreme Court of India in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 (5) Mh.L.J. 775, the deduction should be 1/4th when the number of dependents are four (4) to six (6).

sentences.text: Thus, there will be deduction of 1/4th towards the dependency.

8. In view of above discussion, the amount of compensation is calculated as under :-
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY
i. Monthly income of deceased Rs.34,190/- P.M. ii

Annual Income Rs.4,10,280/-
iv Multiply (ii) X (iii) Rs.57,43,920/-
v 1/4th deduction of Rs.57,43,920/- as Rs.14,35,980/-
 deceased vi After Deduction 1/4th of (v) Rs.43,07,940/-

vii Future prospects of 30 % (vi) Rs.12,92,382/-
Total loss of earning (vi) (+) future prospects Rs.56,00,322/-
(vii) COMPENSATION PAYABLE ON OTHER CONVENTIONAL HEADS a) Loss of Filial Consortium to appellant no.1 Rs.2,00, 000/-
to 5 each having Rs.40,000/-
b) Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
c) Loss of Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
Total compensation (Rs.56,00,322/- as a loss of Rs.58,30,322/-
earning & future prospects (+) Rs.2,30,000/- as on account of other heads)
9.
The learned Tribunal computed the compensation of Rs.41,06,200/- and the above calculations show that, that compensation comes to Rs. 58,30,322/-.
There is enhancement to the extent of Rs.17,24,122/-.

The amount towards enhanced compensation be deposited by the Respondent Yasmeen Jahan W/O. Nisar Ahmed And ... vs Vinod S/O. Pralhad Dhule And Others on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65839305/
3 No.1/Insurance Company within eight (8) weeks.
The compensation amount, already deposited by the Insurance Company under the award, is permitted to be withdraw by the Claimants along with interest accrued thereon after following due process.

Rest of the award in respect of interest etc.
remains intact.
The deficit court fees, on the enhanced amount of compensation, be paid in this Court within four (4) weeks.
10. First Appeal stands disposed of accordingly.
No order as to costs.
